From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@sigcorp.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: SIG: Encryption evidence request — key usage & operator separation

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for taking the SIG intake call last week. As part of our SIG assessment we need a compact evidence bundle around encryption and key management covering:

- KMS access matrix (who has what level of access; role to principal mapping)
- HSM operator separation proof (shift logs, operator-on-duty matrix, and separation of duties policy)
- Key usage samples (sample audit logs showing wrap/unwrap and AEAD ops for Feb 2027)
- Key retention & destruction policy + the canonical KMS rotation schedule for tenant keys
- Transport and at-rest encryption architecture diagram or a short narrative we can attach to the SIG control narrative

Attached is the SigCorp questionnaire (sig_questionnaire_v2.pdf) — if you can point us at an evidence index (CSV or manifest) and a secure drop location that would help us triage. Ideally we’d like the items above by EOD Thursday PST to keep our assessment on track.

Let me know if Redwood needs a mutual NDA amendment or if a one-hour walkthrough next week would be easier.

Thanks,

Daniel Park
Security Analyst, SigCorp
security@sigcorp.com

Attachments: sig_questionnaire_v2.pdf

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. We can get you an evidence index and the most requested artifacts. High-level plan:

1) I attached an evidence manifest (evidence_index.csv) with the items we expect to deliver and who owns each.
2) We'll upload artifacts to a temporary Drive folder (link below) and additionally stage larger logs on an SFTP host you can pull from.
3) Proposed timeline: initial bundle (policy docs + ACL exports + architecture narrative) by Wed EOD PST; HSM shift logs and sampled audit logs by Thu EOD PST.

Internal owners: Marissa (security ops) will pull the HSM operator logs and separation statement; Jonas (platform ops) will export the KMS ACLs and rotation schedule; I’ll prepare the narrative and confirm retention/destruction policy links.

If you prefer a walkthrough, I can book a 30-min window tomorrow morning. Otherwise we’ll send the bundle per the timeline above.

Ben Carter

Marissa / Jonas — forwarding SigCorp ask. Quick breakdown (deliver to the Drive folder above + zip large logs to hsm_shiftlogs_feb2027.zip and place on SFTP):

- Marissa: please produce a one-page "operator separation" attestation (signed by Security Ops lead) describing how HSM operator roles are separated from key custodians and auditors; include Feb 2027 shift logs (hsm_shiftlogs_feb2027.zip) and a sample of operator activity entries.

- Jonas: export KMS ACLs (CSV mapping of service accounts/users -> keyIDs -> roles), provide the tenant key rotation schedule (canonical schedule + last 6 rotation events), and a 1-paragraph retention/destruction summary referencing our policy doc.

Target: initial artifacts by 2027-03-03 17:00 PST so I can validate before we hand to SigCorp on Thu. If either of you need longer, pushback now and I’ll ask for a short extension.

Thanks — Ben

Ben, Marissa, Jonas —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the manifest. The plan you outlined works for us. A couple notes:

- We should avoid sending raw private keys over the drive/SFTP. Sample logs that demonstrate wrap/unwrap events with keyIDs (not key material) are fine.
- For the operator separation attestation, a short bullets list of controls + a signed line from your security ops manager will suffice for the SIG review.
- Once you have the artifacts staged, please add a short readme.txt in the root of the Drive folder listing what is sensitive and where to pull large archives from SFTP.

Can we schedule a 30-min walkthrough Friday 10:00 AM PST to step through the HSM logs and the rotation schedule? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Also, for the audit record, could you include a sample of KMS audit rows showing a rotation event (timestamp, keyID, initiating principal, operation) — redacted for PII if necessary.

Thanks — looking forward to the bundle.

Daniel
